source.title: Upper body of a giant (Klytios?), Pergamon Altar Gigantomachy frieze (plaster cast) - stand-in for Prometheus
source.attribution: Giant from the Pergamon Altar frieze, plaster cast. 3D scan: SMK - Statens Museum for Kunst, Royal Cast Collection (open.smk.dk), public domain.

frame.units: 1.0 = chin-to-crown head height (vertical); source units per head = 40.4396
frame.axes: +Y up = vertical turn axis; +Z = measured gaze (a camera on +Z at eye height is stared at); +X = Y x Z = the figure's own left. L/R in anchor names = the figure's own left/right.
frame.origin: head centre: halfway between chin and crown, on the turn axis through the neck between the ears
frame.restoreCastPosture: rotate head-space geometry about +X by -6.000 deg to restore the cast's own vertical (the gaze then rises 6.00 deg above horizontal)
frame.chin: ESTIMATED (hidden in the beard): from the snapped stomion, stomion-to-chin = 1.68 x nose-tip-to-stomion (vertical) and 0.50 x that distance back, the proportions measured on david and sol

cuts.what: slab return on the +X edge (source x = 62)

frame.cutsNote: capped plane cuts: normal = outward normal of the flat cap (head space), point = a point on the plane. A cap is seen only from cameras on its outward side.

L.measured: visible cap centre (blank eye; biased downward by the overhanging upper lid, not a true gaze - the look direction is +Z by construction)

R.measured: visible cap centre (blank eye; biased downward by the overhanging upper lid, not a true gaze - the look direction is +Z by construction)

torso.neckAxisFit: line fitted through 7 smooth-skin slab centroids under the jaw

shoulders.shoulderL: top of the shoulder 0.06 inside its outer edge
shoulders.shoulderR: top of the shoulder 0.06 inside its outer edge

torso.note: forward/left: horizontal directions the chest faces / its own left (principal axis of the cross-section above the cut); neckAxisUp: line through the neck's smooth-skin cross-section centroids under the jaw (see neckAxisFit). shoulderL/R: from the torso's lateral extremes in the cross-section 0.25 below the chin, the top of the shoulder 0.06 inside each (see shoulders; the casts are cut well inside the real acromion, so this marks the edge of what exists). neckBase: the neck axis at the mean shoulder height, at most chin - 0.12 (approximate, +-0.05; on the bearded giant the throat is hidden by the beard).

bake.ao: channel 0: ambient visibility, 48 cosine-weighted rays per vertex, mean normalised free distance up to 0.25 head units (1 = open, 0 = enclosed)
bake.cavity: channel 1: signed multi-scale curvature, 0.5 = flat, < 0.5 crevice (curl undercuts, eye corners, lid creases, nostrils), > 0.5 ridge/edge; value = 0.5 + 0.5*tanh(c/2.5), c in robust-sigma units
bake.thickness: channel 2: inward free distance along -normal (7-ray 22 deg cone) / 0.12 head units; low = thin (nose wings, ears, lids, curl tips, lips): use for subsurface translucency
bake.skin: channel 3: 1 = broad smooth carved skin (face, neck, chest), 0 = hair/beard/deep carving; use for polish/gloss and SSS strength

notes: Gaze per eye measured relative to the facial symmetry plane (deg, +yaw = figure's left, +pitch = up): {"eyeL": {"yaw": 11.93, "pitch": 0.17}, "eyeR": {"yaw": -11.57, "pitch": 6.99}}.
Facial symmetry plane residual 0.0096 head units (mirror-ICP on the face).
Crop: one horizontal plane at y = -0.95, capped (flat cap facing -Y); keep it out of frame or in shadow.
Turn: yaw about +Y through the origin. The 90-degree turn starts with the camera on the figure's RIGHT (-X side, face pointing screen-right) and ends on +Z (stared at).

Ears: earL ESTIMATED: ear hidden by hair/beard; outer surface point beside the ear position estimated 0.318 behind the eyeball midpoint along the facial axis (ratio measured on david); earR ESTIMATED: ear hidden by hair/beard; outer surface point beside the ear position estimated 0.318 behind the eyeball midpoint along the facial axis (ratio measured on david)
Head units: 1.0 = 40.440 source units (raw STL units).
Mouth anchor (stomion): parted lips: centre of the opening at the depth of the lip fronts.
relief ground slab (source z = 7) cap (outward normal [0.89427, 0.04678, -0.44507]) faces the camera on the turn arc: never
slab return on the +X edge (source x = 62) cap (outward normal [0.44752, -0.09348, 0.88937]) faces the camera on the turn arc: yaw 0-63
STAND-IN: the giant (Klytios?) from the Pergamon Altar Gigantomachy; no freely licensed scan of a marble Prometheus exists. Same Hellenistic pathos face family as Laocoon and Adam's Prometheus.

Relief slab removed: cut at source z = 7 (relief ground, a big flat cap behind the head and back) and x = 62 (its return, which cuts through the figure's left shoulder: a slanted flat face beside the beard, lower right of frame at yaw 0). Approach the profile ONLY from the -X side (see the cap visibility notes and frame.cuts); keep the shoulder cap out of frame or in shadow in the last, frontal inserts. The arms are broken off (no hands).
Blank eyes. Yaw = mean of the two eyeball caps (0.2 deg); pitch 6.0 deg chosen visually (renders at camera pitch -15..+25); head space is levelled.
The chin is hidden in the beard: anchors.chin is an ESTIMATE (frame.chin); anchors.beardTip is the lowest point of the beard. Head units therefore use an anatomical chin, not the beard tip.
